title: benchmarks.py run --dry-run starts claude --version: Bench.__init__ probes the Claude Code version before any plan
goal: A --dry-run of python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run starts no claude at all, a claude --version included: bench_core.Bench reads the Claude Code version only when a scenario writes a row, so a plan that says no model is started starts no program of claude either

run: import os,subprocess,sys,tempfile; t=tempfile.mkdtemp(); b=os.path.join(t,'bin'); os.mkdir(b); log=os.path.join(t,'log'); open(os.path.join(b,'claude'),'w').write('#!/bin/sh\necho x >> '+log+'\n'); os.chmod(os.path.join(b,'claude'),0o755); subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/benchmarks.py','run','pool','--dry-run','--sample','1'],capture_output=True,env=dict(os.environ,PATH=b+os.pathsep+os.environ['PATH'])); sys.exit(1 if os.path.exists(log) else 0)

gates.question: How does a --dry-run start no claude --version: lazy Bench.cc plus a dry run reading ?, or move the probe out of Bench.__init__ only?
options: Bench.cc is a lazy property, ? under a dry run, benchmarks.py presets ? for --paid

gates.recommendation: Bench.cc is a lazy property, ? under a dry run, benchmarks.py presets ? for --paid
gates.reason: bench_pool reads getattr(b, cc) before its dry-run branch, outside the touches, so the property itself must not probe then
